# Vaso

> Liquid glass for React. `<Vaso>` refracts the live page behind an element through a physically based lens (squircle bezel, Snell's law, spectral dispersion), with a backdrop-copy fallback for Safari and Firefox. One component, no dependencies besides React 18 or 19.

## References

- [Live examples](https://vaso-react.vercel.app/)
- [Lab: experimental effects, not in the package yet](https://vaso-react.vercel.app/lab)
- [README](https://github.com/huozhi/vaso/blob/main/README.md)
- [Source and issues](https://github.com/huozhi/vaso)
- [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/vaso)

## Install

```bash
npm add vaso
```

`vaso` is a client component (`'use client'`). In frameworks with server components, render it from a client component.

## Quick start

```tsx
import { Vaso } from 'vaso'

export function Toolbar() {
  return (
    <Vaso radius={24} depth={1.2} blur={0.5} dispersion={0.6} outset={{ x: 8, y: 4 }}>
      <button>Share</button>
    </Vaso>
  )
}
```

The glass sizes itself to its children and refracts whatever is painted behind it. It needs something behind it to bend: text, an image, a gradient. On a flat color it looks like a plain rim.

## Props

All standard HTML attributes (className, style, onClick, ...) pass through to the root element.

| Prop | Type | Default | Range | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | ReactNode | – | – | Content on top of the glass. Without children, set `width` and `height` |
| `component` | string \| ComponentType | `'div'` | – | Root element, e.g. `'span'` for inline glass |
| `width` / `height` | number | content size | – | Explicit size in px |
| `outset` | number \| `{ x, y, top, right, bottom, left }` | `0` | – | Extends the glass past the element without affecting layout. Sides beat axes |
| `radius` | number | element's CSS `border-radius` | 0–∞ | Corner radius. Leave it out to follow classes like `rounded-full` |
| `depth` | number | `0` | −5 to 5 | Refraction strength at the bezel. Negative = concave (compresses). `0` = flat, no refraction |
| `blur` | number | `0.1` | 0–10 | Backdrop blur in px. High values read as frosted glass |
| `dispersion` | number \| false | `0.5` | 0–3 | Rainbow split along the refracting edge. Fades out as depth → 0 |
| `specular` | number \| false | `0.5` | 0–1 | Rim highlight intensity |
| `px` / `py` | number | – | – | Deprecated, use `outset={{ x, y }}` |

Exports: `Vaso`, and the types `VasoProps`, `Outset`.

## Recipes

Button or pill around content:

```tsx
<Vaso className="rounded-full" depth={1.4} outset={4}>
  <span>Dark</span>
</Vaso>
```

Lens over an image (no children, explicit size, positioned over the content):

```tsx
<div style={{ position: 'relative' }}>
  <img src="/photo.jpg" />
  <Vaso width={120} height={120} radius={60} depth={2.5} style={{ position: 'absolute', left: 40, top: 40 }} />
</div>
```

Concave lens: `<Vaso width={60} height={60} radius={30} depth={-4} dispersion={1.5} />`

Frosted panel: `<Vaso radius={20} depth={0.3} blur={6} specular={0.9}>…</Vaso>`

Good starting values: controls `depth 1–1.5, blur 0.3–1`; lenses `depth 2–3`; panels `depth 0.2–0.5, blur 4–8`.

## How it renders

- Chromium (Chrome, Edge, Arc, Opera): an SVG displacement filter inside `backdrop-filter` refracts the real backdrop.
- Safari, Firefox and every iOS browser: Vaso clones the nearest ancestor with visible content into the glass and refracts the copy, kept aligned every frame. Sources over 400 elements aren't cloned; the glass keeps its blur and rim.

## Gotchas

- An ancestor with `filter`, `opacity` < 1, `mask`, `clip-path`, `mix-blend-mode` or its own `backdrop-filter` becomes the backdrop boundary in Chromium: the glass only sees content inside that ancestor.
- `depth={0}` (the default) means no refraction. Set a depth to see the effect.
- Animating the size is fine: Vaso stretches the last displacement map while the size changes and redraws once it settles.

## Performance

- Each dispersion band is a full displacement pass (up to 9 in Chromium). For large glass, or many glass elements at once, use `dispersion={false}` or a low value.
- Large `blur` on large glass is the next biggest cost.
- Prefer a few glass elements over dozens; each one is its own compositing layer.
